title: The Promise of the Crescent Cove
premise: Mirabel Delacroix, a pastry chef hiding from a family that once broke him, hires a stranger to pose as his boyfriend at the Delacroix reunion at Crescent Cove. The stranger, Theo, is charming, perceptive—and secretly the developer's son sent to buy out the cove, including Mirabel's café. As their fake romance turns real over one long weekend of shared memories and exposed lies, Mirabel must choose between the survival money Theo can offer and the truth that could destroy them both; in the end, Theo walks away from his father's empire, Mirabel signs nothing, and they reopen the café together as the last train leaves without either of them.
about_author: Wren Hartwell is a former line cook who traded kitchen heat for the quieter warmth of love stories set in small coastal towns. They write about people who rebuild themselves from what survives.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In his failing café, Mirabel bakes through the night to outrun eviction notices, then receives his mother's summons to the Delacroix reunion—where he's expected with a plus-one. Desperate and half-drunk on exhaustion, he asks Theo, a regular customer who always orders alone, to be his fake boyfriend. Emotional beat: fear disguised as practicality, and the first crack in Mirabel's armor.

chapters.title: The Reunion at Crescent Cove
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. At the family estate, Theo performs the perfect boyfriend so well it unsettles Mirabel, while Theo privately meets with surveyors—he's scouting the cove for his father's resort bid. A stolen moment on the beach after dessert feels dangerously real. Emotional beat: longing blooming inside a lie, with dramatic irony tightening around Theo's secret.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings Back
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Old family letters reveal Mirabel was disinherited for protecting the cove once before, and Theo realizes his father's deal will destroy him. When Mirabel discovers the development contract in Theo's bag, the weekend detonates: accusations, confessions, and Mirabel choosing pride over the rescue money. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief colliding—the climax where love and survival become opposites.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, closing with Theo's. Mirabel returns to sign the café away, but finds Theo has already refused his inheritance and bought the café's debt himself—not as charity, but as partnership. On the empty platform, Mirabel finally lets someone stay past the last train. Emotional beat: release and renewal; memory reclaimed not as loss, but as foundation.
